data.name: Hint
data.value: If the company uses part of your home as its office, it can rent that part from you, unfurnished, under a lease. It pays the rent out of its profit, before your pay, and deducts it. The rent is never pay: you are taxed on it with your pay, without social contributions, on the rent or, when the rent is under the floor the law sets, on that floor, less flat charges.

data.name: CadastralIncomeHint
data.value: Not indexed, as your property-tax notice or MyMinfin gives it.

data.name: ShareHint
data.value: The part of your home the company uses, usually by floor area.

data.name: Help_Cap
data.value: At most {0} for the year: {3} of {1}, the cadastral income of the part let, revalued by {2}. Above it, the excess would be taxed as director pay.

data.name: Help_CadastralIncome
data.value: The notional yearly rental income the administration sets for a property, on which its property tax is computed.

data.name: Help_Floor
data.value: The rent is under the floor, so you are taxed on the floor: the cadastral income of the part let, indexed by {0}, plus {1}.

data.name: Help_FlatCharges
data.value: A flat deduction for maintenance and repairs in place of real costs: {0} of what you are taxed on, the floor when the rent is under it, at most {1} of the cadastral income of the part let, revalued by {2}.

data.name: Help_JoinsTaxableIncome
data.value: Netto taxes all of it in your column, as if the home were yours alone. A home you own with your partner is shared by law, half each under community of property, by your shares otherwise: Netto does not split it yet.

data.name: Remove
data.value: Remove home office rent from your plan
